chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Ibn Bukayr, and others, said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was performing the circumambulation (Tawaf), so he looked towards a group at the side of the Masjid and said, 'What is this group?' They said, 'This is Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri. His intellect is muddled, so he does not speak. His family brought him out, hoping that when he sees the people, he will speak.'
So when Ali ibn al-Husayn finished his Tawaf, he went out until he approached him. When Muhammad ibn Shihab saw him, he recognized him.
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'I was appointed to a governorship, so I shed blood. I killed a man, so what you see has entered me.'
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I am more fearful for you regarding your despair from the Mercy of Allah than I am fearful for you regarding what you have done.'

Then he said to him, 'Give them the blood money (Diyah).' He said, 'I have done it, but they refused.' So he said, 'Make it into small packages, then watch the times of the Prayers, and throw them into their houses.'

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation for killing

ai.seo_question: What did Ali ibn al-Husayn advise Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri to do after he killed a man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the transition of Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri from a rational scholar to one afflicted by guilt after killing a man, illustrating the Shia emphasis on practical repentance (Tawbah) over mere despair. Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) advises him that despairing of God's mercy is more detrimental than the sin itself, and prescribes a unique method of paying blood money (Diyah) by discreetly placing it in the victims' homes during prayer times to ensure acceptance and facilitate spiritual peace.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, and Ibn Bukeyr and someone else who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was in the circumambulation (of the Kaaba), so he<sup>asws</sup> looked at a group around the Masjid. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is this group?’ So they said, ‘This is Muhammad Bin Shihab Al-Zahry. His intellect is muddled up, so he does not speak. So his family have brought him out, perhaps when he sees the people he would speak’.

So when Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> fulfilled his<sup>asws</sup> circumambulation, he<sup>asws</sup> went out until he<sup>asws</sup> approached him. So when Muhammad Bin Shihab saw him<sup>asws</sup>, he recognised him<sup>asws</sup>.

So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘What is the matter with you?’ So he said, ‘I was given the governorship, so I shed blood. I killed a man, so there entered into me what you<sup>asws</sup> see’.
So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> have more intense fear of your despair from the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from what you have come to’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give them the wergild’. He said, ‘I have done it, but they refused (to accept it)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Make it as small packages, then wait for the timings of the Prayers, so throw these in their houses’.
